title: Coherent right-fibration classifier and its Day convolution pullback
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], right fibrations and their space-valued classification of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], cocartesian unstraightening of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], and cartesian monoidal envelopes of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'\in\mathcal U''$. Write $\mathcal S$ for $\mathcal U$-small spaces and $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ for $\mathcal U$-small infinity categories; categories of presheaves and right fibrations are formed in the larger universes. Let $\operatorname{RFib}$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U})$ on right fibrations, and $p=\operatorname{ev}_1:\operatorname{RFib}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$. Its morphisms are coherent commutative squares of right fibrations, with all higher simplices retained.

The functor $p$ is both cartesian and cocartesian. Its fibre at $D$ is $P(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. For $h:D\to D'$, cartesian transport is restriction $h^*$, cartesian arrows are pullback squares, and cocartesian transport is left Kan extension along $h^{\mathrm{op}}$. Finite products in $\operatorname{RFib}$ are products of arrows; $p$ preserves them, including the terminal arrow $*\to *$. A product of right fibrations for $F_i:D_i^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ classifies the external product $(d_i)\mapsto\prod_iF_i(d_i)$.

For every infinity category $K$ and coherent diagram $D:K\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ fitting in the containing universes, let $X_D\to K$ be the cocartesian unstraightening of $k\mapsto D(k)^{\mathrm{op}}$. There is a natural equivalence of infinity categories
$$\{D\}\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U})}\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{RFib})\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(X_D,\mathcal S).$$
The left side is the infinity-categorical fibre, so it retains a specified coherent identification with $D$. It has all sections, with no cartesian or cocartesian preservation condition. Under this equivalence a section $\Phi$ has value at $(k,d)$ equal to the fibre at $d$ of the right fibration $\Phi(k)\to D(k)$. The equivalence includes transformations, their mapping spaces and all higher simplices, and is natural under base change in $K$ and pullback along transformations of diagrams $D$.

Put $S=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and pull all cartesian envelopes below back along the ordered-block functor $S\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$. This functor takes $[r]$ to $\langle r\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,r\}$ and, for the opposite ordinal map $a:[s]\to[r]$ of a base arrow $[r]\to[s]$, sends $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to $j$ if $a(j-1)<i\leq a(j)$ and to the basepoint otherwise; thus the retained block of output $j$ is $I_j=\{a(j-1)+1,\ldots,a(j)\}$, possibly empty. The induced functor
$$p^\times:\operatorname{RFib}^\times\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^\times$$
is a cocartesian fibration. Its fibre at a tuple $(D_1,\ldots,D_r)$ is $\prod_iP(D_i)$. For a base arrow with retained blocks $I_j$ and block functors $b_j:\prod_{i\in I_j}D_i\to D'_j$, its cocartesian transport takes $(F_i)$ to the left Kan extensions of $\prod_{i\in I_j}F_i$ along $b_j^{\mathrm{op}}$. The empty block uses $*\to D'_j$ and the terminal space. All these assertions concern actual coherent cartesian envelopes and their pullbacks.

For every small monoidal infinity category $C$ in the convention of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], let $\underline C:S\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^\times$ be its coherent classifying algebra: over $[r]$ it is the tuple of $r$ copies of $C$, and its block arrows are the tensor functors, including the unit. The infinity-categorical pullback
$$Q_C=S\times_{\underline C,\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^\times,p^\times}\operatorname{RFib}^\times$$
is a monoidal cocartesian fibration with fibre $P(C)^r$. Its operations are Day convolution, namely the left Kan extensions of the external products along the opposite tensor functors of $C$, including the nullary operation. An arrow of $Q_C$ over an inert base arrow is cocartesian if and only if its image in $\operatorname{RFib}^\times$ is inert. The section-classification equivalence displayed above is valid for the universal product right fibration over $Q_C$ as well, after increasing only the containing universe. In particular it gives a coherent space-valued evaluation on $Q_C\times_S C^{\mathrm{op},\otimes}$, with value $\prod_iF_i(c_i)$ at $((F_i),(c_i))$. This evaluation and all its higher simplices are natural under restriction in the base and under strong monoidal functors of $C$; the induced presheaf restriction is lax monoidal. No equivalence with an essential-image subset of an unmarked relative exponential is asserted.
